title: GS21 with the priced y factor on production, exposure = standardized PRODUCTIVITY (gvyz10), and a FIXED capital structure with NO refinancing: three leverage types born with coupon 0.158, 0.421 or 0.684 per unit capital, new debt issued pari passu at investment, drawn independently of productivity
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is a PRODUCT of a hidden type and a within-firm state, so the premium is an interaction the ranks cannot span?
notes: 2026-10-22. gs_fixcs = 1, xi = 0 in gs_solve_vy.py / gs_sim_vy.py: no refinancing event ever; at investment the firm issues new debt at the same coupon per unit capital and equity receives (1 - kappa_b)(g - 1) Q(b); old debt's value per old unit is unchanged. Leverage is the type for the firm's whole life (D/E about 0.25 / 1.0 / 3.25). Replaces gvyzl (diluting coupons) and gvyzlx (monthly costless refinancing, no convergence).

changes: gs_bv [0.1, 0.1, 0.1] x (gs_bzl 0.0 + gs_bzi 1.0 z~): type x productivity exposure, bv_comp 0.0
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv (gs_bzl + gs_bzi z~) y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
